title: Platform audit read — wire shapes, version 1
description: The machine-readable half of platform-audit-read-v1.contract.yaml. BOTH ARE NORMATIVE TOGETHER. Nothing in this repository executes JSON Schema, so every constraint here is READ BY A PERSON AND HAND-IMPLEMENTED: a `required` list is an instruction someone will follow literally (.claude/rules/workflow.md §12). THE TWO RECORD SHAPES BELOW DIFFER BY EXACTLY ONE FIELD AND THAT DIFFERENCE IS THE SECURITY PROPERTY OF THIS CONTRACT.

platformRole.description: The actor's platform role AT THE TIME OF THE ACTION, recorded on the row rather than resolved at read time — a role that changed later must not rewrite history.

actionId.description: Which platform operation was invoked, e.g. 'platform.credentials.reset'. A stable token, never a human sentence — a log a machine cannot group is a log nobody can review.

outcome.description: TWO VALUES, NOT A CODE. A reason string would drift toward describing WHAT went wrong, and 0025 Decision 5 forbids the contents of what was touched. Note that 'failed' here means the operation failed AFTER the authority check — a caller who is not an established operator writes no record at all (platform-operator-v1 whichSIDEOFTHEAUTHORITYCHECKTHEWRITESITSON), so this log contains no evidence of probing by non-operators. That blind spot is recorded there, not solved here.

recordCommon.description: NOT A STANDALONE SHAPE — the fields both feeds share. Nothing here names a customer, a Workspace, a field value, a diff, an Organization name, a Template name, or any credential material, and none may be added: 0025 Decision 5 permits the operation and its target identifiers and NOTHING ELSE, because 'an operator log that accumulates customer data is a second copy of the tenant database with weaker access rules.'

record_id.description:
Opaque. It is the tiebreaker in the (occurred_at, record_id) sort key, which is why it is on the wire at all — paging over a non-unique timestamp alone either skips records or repeats them, and an audit feed that silently skips a record is worse than one that refuses to page.

CORRECTED 2026-09-05. This justification previously said 'a SECOND-precision timestamp'. CORE WRITES MILLISECONDS — kernel/clock.ts::toRfc3339Utc is new Date(ms).toISOString(), which always emits .sssZ, and nothing truncates. THE CONCLUSION IS RE-DERIVED AND HOLDS MORE STRONGLY, not less: on Workers the clock DOES NOT ADVANCE DURING EXECUTION (docs/decisions/0015 finding 3 — 'Date.now() returns the time of the last I/O'), so two records written between the same pair of I/O operations have an IDENTICAL millisecond timestamp deterministically, not by coincidence. The tiebreaker is therefore load-bearing under exactly the conditions that produce the most records. Do not remove it as redundant.

actor_principal_id.description: WHICH OPERATOR ACTED. Disclosing this is not a leak: operators are a known set to anyone who can read this feed at all, and identifying the actor is the entire point of an operator log.

correlation_id.description: Ties this record to the request that produced it and to the tenant-side record written alongside it. It is the only identifier that crosses the two audit homes, and it is what makes a two-database trail reconstructable after a partial failure.

platformFeedRecord.description: THE PLATFORM FEED RECORD. IT HAS NO `target_principal_id` AND MUST NEVER GAIN ONE — that is the single field whose presence would let this feed aggregate into the CO1 mapping organization-detail-v1's theMembershipRuling refuses: every resolve record is 'principal P was resolved in Organization O', which is a membership fact, and a bulk read would collect every one of them in a single request the affected tenants cannot see. THE ORGANIZATION-LEVEL TARGET IS FINE, because an operator can enumerate Organizations from their own home screen and learning that one was acted on discloses nothing they could not obtain there.

target_organization_id.description: Null for an action that names no Organization — a Template create, or a whoami. REQUIRED AND NULLABLE rather than optional, so a client never has to distinguish 'absent' from 'none'.

organizationFeedRecord.description: THE ORGANIZATION FEED RECORD. It carries `target_principal_id`, and it may BECAUSE THE CALLER NAMED THE ORGANIZATION — the identical gate the membership ruling applies to the resolve: an operator must already have a reason to ask about a specific customer. There is no `target_organization_id` here because the path parameter already fixed it, and repeating it would invite a client to trust the body over the path.

target_principal_id.description: The principal the action named — the person a credential was reset for, or the one a resolve returned. Null for an action naming no principal. THIS IS THE FIELD THE PLATFORM FEED OMITS.

cursor.description: Opaque, BOUND TO THE PRINCIPAL AND TO THE QUERY SHAPE. Never constructed or parsed by a client. Principal-bound so one operator cannot resume another's enumeration of a record of everyone's activity; query-shape-bound so a cursor issued by the Organization feed CANNOT BE SPENT ON THE PLATFORM FEED — otherwise the one-field difference between the two record shapes could be crossed by replaying a cursor, which is the substitution property confirmation-v1's binding relies on, applied to pagination. Null means no further page.
